name: Arms
description: The disciplined use of a weapon: distance, timing, and knowing when the fight is already lost.

name: Athletics
description: Carrying, climbing, holding a door shut against someone who wants it open. What you can lift includes what a body weighs.

name: Endurance
description: Going without. Hunger and thirst arrive on the same schedule for everyone; they simply cost you less on the way.

name: Stealth
description: Not being where attention is. Half of what keeps a crime from acquiring a witness (D-217).

name: Perception
description: Noticing the thing at the edge — a shape at a window, a hand near a purse, a door that was shut before.

name: Medicine
description: Packing, binding and stitching. Major wounds cannot be treated by the wounded, so this skill is a debt other people owe you (D-205).

name: Craft
description: Joinery, smithing, tanning, baking — the trades collapsed into one habit of hand. Work goes faster and wastes less.

name: Survival
description: Reading ground, weather and spoor. Where a thing grows, where a seam runs, and which way is home after dark.

name: Bluff
description: Saying a false thing as though it were true. Contested by another's Insight whenever you declare a name that is not yours (D-218).

name: Insight
description: Reading the person, not the words. Tells you that something is off — never what the truth is, and it is wrong often enough to hurt.

name: Intimidation
description: Making it plain what happens if you are refused. Cheaper than violence, and remembered longer.

name: Persuasion
description: Giving someone a reason they can repeat to themselves afterwards. The only tool that leaves the other party believing it was their idea.

name: Lore
description: What the empire was, whose family held which seal, and which of the old names are still dangerous to say aloud.

name: Attunement
description: The capacity to hold a working steady while something in the room objects. Not power — patience under pressure.

name: Necromancy
description: The traffic between a body and what has left it. Scales how many dead you can hold upright at once (D-511).
